extracted.intended_audience: agency adjudication managers, hearing examiners, agency legal staff, and policy analysts tracking administrative hearing performance
extracted.subtask_short: agency hearing timelines and service rules
extracted.subtask_description: This page provides procedural metrics and standards for administrative adjudication hearings (timing, hearing length, use of prehearing conferences, examiner workload) and illustrative agency rules on service of process and subpoenas across federal agencies. It is intended to guide measurement, reporting, and procedural compliance for agency hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length of time from assignment to examiner to decision by examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: Measured as number of proceedings falling into time bands from initial assignment to examiner to the examiner's decision in proceedings in which examiners issued decisions on the merits after evidentiary hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time bands used: 1 month or less; 1 to 3 months; 3 to 6 months; 6 to 12 months; over 12 months. Tables break counts out by agency and type of proceeding. Footnotes note exceptions in computation (e.g., Federal Maritime Board computed from time directed to hold hearing rather than initial assignment) and indicate cases with missing data or defaults; grand totals reported (e.g., 11,696 proceedings across 21 agencies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Length of time from assignment to examiner to opening of the hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Measured counts of proceedings by interval between assignment to the examiner and the opening of the hearing, categorized into the same time bands as above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time bands: 1 month or less; 1 to 3 months; 3 to 6 months; 6 to 12 months; over 12 months. Tables provide per-agency, per-proceeding-type counts. Footnotes explain unavailable divisions for some bulk data and special-case computations for particular agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time from close of hearing to final submission to examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of proceedings by interval between the close of the hearing and the final submission to the examiner (i.e., when the record is finally submitted for decision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time bands used in tables: 15 days or less; 16–30 days; 31–60 days; 61–90 days; over 90 days. Data are reported by agency and proceeding type. Footnotes note instances where data were not available or where only aggregate hours/days are reported instead of the full band breakdown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time from final submission to examiner to issuance of examiner's decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of proceedings by interval between the examiner's receipt of final submission and the issuance of the examiner's decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time bands used: 15 days or less; 16–30 days; 31–60 days; 61–90 days; 91 days to 6 months; over 6 months. Tables show per-agency distributions. Footnotes indicate cases where periods were unavailable or estimates were used; some agencies reported total hours instead of days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prehearing conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether and how often prehearing conferences were held — counted as number of cases in which prehearing conferences were held (listed per agency and proceeding type).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables list number of cases in which prehearing conferences were held alongside total cases disposed of on the merits after hearing. Interpretation should account for agency practices; some agencies report frequent use while others report few or none.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cases suspended on interlocutory appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of cases that were suspended while interlocutory appeals were pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables show number of cases suspended on interlocutory appeals per agency and proceeding type. These suspensions affect elapsed-time metrics and are tracked separately in the performance tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average number of days of hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Average duration of hearings (reported as average number of days per proceeding) for each agency/proceeding type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some agencies report total hours rather than days (footnotes indicate when hours are reported). Averages are provided in tables (e.g., mean number of days of hearing); interpret with caution where number-of-days breakdown is incomplete or where long hearings were recorded as total hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cases in which the hearing was reopened prior to examiner's decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of proceedings in which the hearing record was reopened before the examiner issued the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables provide per-agency counts; footnotes clarify that some reopened hearings were later remanded or had no separate time data furnished, so totals may include cases without full time-interval breakdowns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total hours/days in hearing (aggregate hearing time)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate measure of hearing time for groups of cases (total hours in hearing across cases) reported for some agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnotes note total hours in hearing where available (e.g., total hours in hearing in 2,276 cases was 13,656) and when number-of-days-on-which-hearings-were-held is not available. Use aggregate hours to complement average-day metrics where detailed banding is missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing examiner staffing and man-years available
rubrics_metrics.description: Staffing metrics: number of examiners employed (start and end of period), number borrowed from or loaned to other agencies, and total man-years available to the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table IX reports these staffing counts by agency and includes explanatory footnotes (e.g., training time, inclusion/exclusion of certain examiners). Use these to normalize workload and time metrics (e.g., decisions per man-year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Average number of days in hearings and pre-hearing conferences per man-year (examiner workload)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average days per man-year that examiners spent in hearings and pre-hearing conferences, reported by agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess examiner workload intensity. Table IX provides values per agency and notes exceptions (e.g., some agencies report hours instead). Training, travel, and other non-hearing time may affect these figures; footnotes sometimes explain inclusions/exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average number of decisions on the merits per man-year
rubrics_metrics.description: Average number of examiner decisions on the merits produced per man-year, by agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table IX reports decisions per man-year; footnotes point out that some decisions are consent or default decisions (e.g., a stated percent of FTC decisions were consent decisions; a portion of Post Office decisions were defaults), which affects interpretation of decision-count productivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total proceedings assigned for conduct of hearing only
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of proceedings assigned to examiners for the conduct of hearing only (i.e., hearings where examiners conducted hearings but may not have issued decisions counted under the same metric).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table IX provides totals by agency; useful for measuring hearing workload distinct from decision-writing workload. Footnotes clarify certain special assignments and exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of process — By whom served
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrative rule: the agency shall serve all orders, notices and other papers it issues and is required by law to serve; every other paper shall be served by the party filing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the President's Conference illustrative rule. It places primary responsibility for serving agency-generated papers on the agency and for party-filed papers on the filing party; local agency rules may vary as shown in the preceding agency-by-agency table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of process — Upon whom served
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrative rule: papers shall be served upon all counsel of record and upon parties not represented by counsel or their designated agents; any counsel entering an appearance after initiation must notify other counsel and unrepresented parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables of agency rules corroborate that agencies routinely require service on counsel of record and unrepresented parties or their agents. The illustrative rule emphasizes full notice to all participants and filing counsel's duty to notify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of process — Method of service
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrative rule: methods of service include personal delivery or, unless prohibited by law, first-class or registered mail, telegraph, or publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The illustrative rule enumerates acceptable methods; the agency-specific table shows variations among agencies and cites governing regulations (e.g., 17 CFR § 0.22(b), 7 CFR § 900.69(b), 14 CFR §§ 301.6, 302.8, etc.). Use agency-specific rule citations for compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of process — When service is complete
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrative rule: service by mail is complete upon deposit in the U.S. mail properly stamped and addressed; by telegraph when deposited with a telegraph company properly addressed with charges prepaid; by publication when due notice has been given in the publication as required by law or rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines the moment of 'service complete' for timing and procedural deadlines. Agency tables and footnotes should be consulted for variations or statutory exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of process — Filing with agency (what constitutes filing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrative rule: papers required to be filed with the agency are deemed filed upon actual receipt by the agency at the place specified in its rules accompanied by proof of service upon required parties; upon such actual receipt the filing date is deemed the date of deposit in the mail or with the telegraph company as provided above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ties together service and filing: actual receipt plus proof of service is required, and for dating purposes the deposit date in mail/telegraph may control. Agency rules may add specifics about addresses and proof-of-service forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency provisions on subpoenas — service and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies maintain rules governing service of subpoenas and statutory fee allowances (table lists, by agency, whether subpoena service and fee provisions exist and their basic parameters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The table headings indicate entries for Service and Fees; details vary by agency and are given in the full table (only partially visible in this chunk). Practitioners should consult the agency-specific citation in the table and footnotes for exact subpoena-service methods, fee schedules, and any special procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and computation notes for time-interval metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnoted rules and exceptions that define exactly how time intervals are computed and note special cases or missing data (e.g., different start points used by some agencies, cases pending before examiners with incomplete interval data, or aggregate reporting instead of banded counts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnotes must be consulted when using the timing metrics: examples include the Federal Maritime Board computing intervals from direction to hold a hearing rather than initial assignment, Social Security partial data on pending cases, and numerous notes indicating excluded cases or estimated figures. Accurate interpretation requires applying these footnote clarifications.
